set.login.ldapHint: You can sign in with your {{name}} account.
set.login.localModeHint: Local sign-in – for administrators only, e.g. when the sign-in service is unavailable.
set.login.sso2faHint: Signing in via {{name}} succeeded. Please enter the code from your authenticator app.
set.login.ssoError.accountDisabled: Your account is disabled in the panel.
set.login.ssoError.config: Single sign-on is not fully configured. Please inform your administrator.
set.login.ssoError.disabled: Single sign-on is currently not enabled.
set.login.ssoError.discovery: The sign-in service cannot be reached. Please try again later.
set.login.ssoError.idToken: The response from the sign-in service was invalid. Please inform your administrator.
set.login.ssoError.idpError: The sign-in service cancelled the sign-in (code: {{code}}).
set.login.ssoError.internal: An internal error occurred during sign-in. Details are in the server log.
set.login.ssoError.linkConflict: This identity is already linked to another panel account.
set.login.ssoError.linkFailed: Linking could not be completed. Please start it again in the settings.
set.login.ssoError.noAccount: No access has been set up in the panel for this account. Please contact your administrator.
set.login.ssoError.notAllowed: Your account is not authorized for this panel (missing group membership).
set.login.ssoError.state: The sign-in has expired or was started in another window. Please start again.
set.login.ssoError.token: The sign-in could not be completed (code exchange failed). Please try again or inform your administrator.
set.login.ssoError.totp_unreadable: Sign-in succeeded, but the 2FA secret of your account cannot be decrypted. Please ask an administrator to reset your 2FA.
set.settings.externalAccountHint: This account signs in via {{source}}. Username and email address are managed there; the display name is taken over on every sign-in if the provider supplies it.
set.settings.externalPasswordHint: The password is managed by the sign-in service ({{source}}) and cannot be changed here.
set.settings.integrations.passkeysExternal: Passkeys are not available for accounts with SSO or LDAP sign-in – sign-in goes through the sign-in service.
set.settings.integrations.ssoLinkBadUrl: The sign-in service did not return a valid address.
set.settings.integrations.ssoLinkConfirm: I understand that sign-in will then only be possible via the company sign-in.
set.settings.integrations.ssoLinkHint: Link your local account with the company sign-in. Zone permissions and settings are kept.
set.settings.integrations.ssoLinkWarning: Afterwards you can no longer sign in with your current password or passkeys; existing passkeys are removed. 2FA and API tokens are kept.
set.settings.integrations.totpDisableExterna: To turn it off, a current code from the authenticator app is enough.
set.settings.integrations.totpUnreadable: 2FA is enabled, but the secret cannot be decrypted.
set.settings.integrations.totpUnreadableHint: The server encryption key was probably changed. Turning it off or setting it up again is only possible via an administrator (“Reset 2FA”); until then, sign-in only works with a passkey.
set.settings.sso.allowLinking: Allow users to link their local account themselves
set.settings.sso.allowLinkingHint: Under Settings → API & security, confirmed with the current password. Afterwards, only sign-in via this service is possible.
set.settings.sso.allowedEmailDomainsHint: Alternative to groups: users may sign in if their email address confirmed by the provider (email_verified) ends exactly in one of these domains, e.g. example.com (no subdomains).
set.settings.sso.baseUrlMissing: No public base URL set. OIDC can only be enabled once it is configured under Settings → Profile.
set.settings.sso.bindDn: Bind DN of the service account
set.settings.sso.caCertHint: Empty = system certificate store. If set, only this CA is trusted.
set.settings.sso.claimHint: Nested claims with a dot, e.g. realm_access.roles. Empty = do not use.
set.settings.sso.displayNameHint: Shown on the sign-in page as “Sign in with …”.
set.settings.sso.groupDnInvalid: Not a full DN (at least two components, e.g. CN=…,OU=…): {{groups}}
set.settings.sso.groupFilterHint: {user_dn} is replaced by the user's DN. Nested AD groups: (member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={user_dn})
set.settings.sso.insecureAllowed: SSO_ALLOW_INSECURE is active: unencrypted connections to the sign-in service are allowed. Use for testing only.
set.settings.sso.issuerHint: e.g. https://sso.example.com/realms/company (Keycloak) or https://auth.example.com/application/o/pdns/ (Authentik). The panel loads /.well-known/openid-configuration from it.
set.settings.sso.jitAllowAny: I confirm: every account of this provider may sign in and automatically gets a panel account.
set.settings.sso.jitAllowAnyHint: Better: enter allowed groups (for OIDC also email domains). The confirmation is recorded in the audit log.
set.settings.sso.jitAllowAnyRequired: Automatic account creation without allowed groups: please enter groups or tick the confirmation.
set.settings.sso.jitEnabled: Create accounts automatically on first sign-in
set.settings.sso.jitEnabledHint: New accounts get the “User” role without zones; an admin assigns zones under Users. Off: only already linked accounts can sign in.
set.settings.sso.jitOpenWarning: Without allowed groups, every account of the provider can sign in (without zone permissions).
set.settings.sso.ldapDisplayNameHint: e.g. “Windows” → “You can sign in with your Windows account.”
set.settings.sso.ldapHint: Users sign in with their directory account in the normal sign-in form. The panel looks up the user with a service account and then checks the password with a bind.
set.settings.sso.loadFailed: Could not load the SSO settings.
set.settings.sso.localLoginEnabled: Allow sign-in with local accounts for all users
set.settings.sso.localLoginEnabledHint: When turned off, only administrators can sign in locally (emergency access). Passkeys, registration and “Forgot password” then also apply to administrators only.
set.settings.sso.oidcHint: For Keycloak, Authentik, Microsoft Entra ID and other OIDC providers. A confidential client with authorization code flow and PKCE is required.
set.settings.sso.presetApplied: Preset applied – please check the issuer URL and client details, then save.
set.settings.sso.reauthNeeded: Not saved: this change requires a fresh sign-in. Sign in again, then save once more.
set.settings.sso.redirectUri: Redirect URI (register it with your identity provider)
set.settings.sso.redirectUriHint: Derived from the public base URL (Settings → Profile). If the base URL changes, update the redirect URI at the provider.
set.settings.sso.requireTotp: After OIDC sign-in, ask for the panel's 2FA (TOTP) if the user has set it up
set.settings.sso.requireTotpHint: Turn this off if your identity provider already enforces multi-factor authentication. For LDAP sign-ins, 2FA always applies.
set.settings.sso.roleModeHint: Applied on every sign-in. The last active admin is never demoted automatically.
set.settings.sso.roleModeOff: No – roles are assigned in the panel only
set.settings.sso.roleModePromote: Promote only – members of the admin groups become admin
set.settings.sso.roleModeSync: Synchronize – admin only while member of an admin group
set.settings.sso.saveFailed: Could not save the SSO settings.
set.settings.sso.secretSet: Saved – leave empty to keep it.
set.settings.sso.secretUnreadable: The saved secret cannot be read (key changed?) – please enter it again.
set.settings.sso.serverUrlsHint: ldaps://dc1.example.local:636 or ldap://ldap.example.local:389. Multiple servers are tried in order.
set.settings.sso.sessionLifetimeHint: Recommendation with SSO: limit the session lifetime (AUTH_COOKIE_MAX_AGE) to 8–24 hours – blocking an account at the sign-in service does not end running panel sessions.
set.settings.sso.sessionLifetimeWarning: A sign-in is currently valid for {{hours}} hours (AUTH_COOKIE_MAX_AGE). With SSO we recommend 8–24 hours: blocking an account at the sign-in service does not end running panel sessions.
set.settings.sso.stepUpHint: Changes to the provider, activation, groups, roles or automatic account creation must be confirmed with your password.
set.settings.sso.stepUpHintExternal: Changes to the provider, activation, groups, roles or automatic account creation are only possible within 10 minutes of your sign-in.
set.settings.sso.subtitle: Sign in via an identity provider (OIDC) or a directory (LDAP/Active Directory).
set.settings.sso.testPasswordHint: With a password, the sign-in is checked as well. The password is not stored.
set.settings.sso.testUsesForm: The values in the form are tested, even if they have not been saved yet.
set.settings.sso.title: Sign-in & single sign-on
set.settings.sso.tlsVerifyHint: Turning this off requires SSO_ALLOW_INSECURE. Better: paste your own CA certificate below.
set.settings.sso.tokenAuthMethod: Client authentication at the token endpoint
set.settings.sso.uniqueIdAttrHint: objectGUID (AD), entryUUID (OpenLDAP), ipaUniqueID (FreeIPA). Empty = DN – the link is then lost if the account is renamed or moved.
set.settings.sso.uniqueIdConfirm: I confirm that this attribute is unique and permanent in the directory.
set.settings.sso.uniqueIdConfirmRequired: The ID attribute is not known to be immutable: please tick the confirmation under “Advanced: attributes”.
set.settings.sso.uniqueIdConfirmWarning: The attribute “{{attr}}” is not known to be immutable (recommended: {{safe}}). If it is changed or reassigned, another directory account can take over an existing panel account.
set.settings.sso.uniqueIdConfirmWarningDn: Without an ID attribute, the DN is used as the identifier (recommended: {{safe}}). Renaming or moving breaks the link, and a new account with the same DN takes it over.
set.settings.sso.useUserinfo: Load additional claims from the UserInfo endpoint
set.settings.sso.userFilterHint: {username} is replaced by the entered name (safely escaped).
set.settings.ssoLinkedSuccess: Account linked with {{source}}. From now on, sign in that way.
set.stepUp.body: This change affects sign-in or the permissions of other users. Please confirm it with your password.
set.stepUp.bodyTotp: This change affects sign-in or the permissions of other users. Please confirm it with your password and the code from your authenticator app.
set.stepUp.reauthBody: Your account signs in via a sign-in service. For this change, your sign-in must not be older than 10 minutes. Sign out and sign in again – afterwards you return to this page automatically and can repeat the change.
set.stepUp.reauthButton: Sign out and sign in again
set.stepUp.title: Confirmation required
set.users.convertReauthNeeded: Not converted: this requires a fresh sign-in. Sign in again and repeat the action.
set.users.convertToLocalHint: Removes the link and assigns a random password (shown once). If automatic account creation is active, this person's next SSO sign-in creates a new account.
set.users.deleteExternalConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? Note: with automatic account creation active, the account is re-created on the next SSO sign-in. To block it permanently, deactivate it instead.
set.users.externalManagedHint: Password, reset link and forced password change are not available for this account – the password is managed by the sign-in service.
set.users.roleManagedBySso: The role is taken from the sign-in service's groups on every sign-in.
